chunks: 2662 - It was narrated from al-Hasan ibn Harun, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: “I ate khabis containing saffron until I was full from it while I was in ihram.”

So he said: “When you complete your rites and want to leave Makkah, buy dates with a dirham and give them in charity. That will be an expiation for that and for whatever may have come upon you in your ihram that you do not know.”

key_terms.تَمْرًا: dates to be purchased and given in charity
key_terms.خَبِيصًا: a sweet dish or confection that was eaten
key_terms.زَعْفَرَانٌ: saffron, a fragrant substance relevant to ihram restrictions
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: a person in the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the kaffarah for eating saffron-containing food while in ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a muhrim who consumed food containing saffron during ihram. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام instructs that after completing the hajj rites and before leaving Makkah, the person should give charity in dates worth one dirham as kaffarah, including for other unknown violations that may have occurred during ihram.
